sections.composition:
I. Kalka Dravyas (Herbal Paste Ingredients) 

 Karvir Mula (Nerium indicum – White Oleander Root) 
 Danti Mula (Baliospermum montanum – Red Physic Nut Root) 
 Haridra (Curcuma longa – Turmeric Rhizome) 
 Langali (Gloriosa superba – Glory Lily Tuber) 
 Chitraka Mula (Plumbago zeylanica – Leadwort Root) 
 Saindhava Lavana (Rock Salt – Natural Mineral Salt) 

 All ingredients are taken in equal proportion and triturated with water to prepare a smooth herbal paste. 
 II. Drava Dravyas (Liquid Ingredients) 

 Bijora Nimbu Svarasa (Citrus medica – Citron Fruit Juice) 
 Arka Kshira (Calotropis gigantea – Giant Milkweed Latex) 

 III. Taila Dravya (Base Oil) 

 Sarshapa Taila (Brassica juncea – Mustard Oil) 

 Method Of Preparation 
 All kalka (paste) dravyas (herbs) are cleaned, dried if required, and finely powdered. The powders are triturated with water to prepare a uniform paste. Mustard oil is taken in a stainless steel vessel and combined with the prepared kalka, measured quantity of Bijora lemon juice (Citrus medica), and Arka latex (Calotropis gigantea). The mixture is heated over mild fire following classical Sneha Paka procedure. Continuous stirring is maintained to prevent burning and to ensure proper integration of ingredients. Heating is continued until the liquid portion evaporates and the oil attains classical signs of completion such as clear oil appearance, characteristic aroma, and non-sticky residue. After natural cooling, the medicated oil is filtered through a clean cloth and stored in airtight glass containers. 
 Method Of Use 

 Local Application – Sterile wick soaked in medicated oil is inserted into the fistulous tract or sinus opening. 
 External Dressing – Applied over affected areas for purification and healing.

 Bhagandara (fistula-in-ano) 
 Nasura (chronic sinus wounds) 
 Deep-seated suppurative lesions 

 Therapeutic Properties 
 Karvir (Nerium indicum) root possesses potent penetrating and cleansing properties that help eliminate unhealthy tissue from deep tracts. Danti (Baliospermum montanum) root enhances purgative and scraping action useful in removing morbid accumulations. Langali (Gloriosa superba) and Chitraka (Plumbago zeylanica) stimulate local metabolism and assist in tissue debridement. Haridra (Curcuma longa) contributes anti-inflammatory and wound-healing activity. Rock salt aids softening and liquefaction of pathological material. Bijora lemon (Citrus medica) juice provides acidic medium enhancing penetration of active principles, while Arka (Calotropis gigantea) latex supports purification and antimicrobial action. Mustard oil acts as a heating and channel-opening base facilitating deep tissue delivery of herbal components. The combined processing through Sneha Paka (oil preparation) produces a potent oil suitable for purification and healing of chronic infected lesions. 
 Method Of Administration 

 The medicated oil is applied locally using sterile wick placement or external dressing under professional supervision. 
 Regular application promotes cleansing of diseased tissue and gradual healing of affected areas.
sections.precautions:
For external therapeutic use under qualified Ayurvedic supervision. 
 Avoid application on healthy tissue or sensitive mucosa. 
 Due to the presence of potent herbs, proper dosage and method should be strictly followed. 

 Conclusion 
 Karvir Taila is a classical Ayurvedic medicated oil prepared with Karvir (Nerium indicum) root, pungent cleansing herbs, acidic juice, and mustard oil through Sneha Paka (oil processing). The formulation is primarily used for local purification and healing in Bhagandara (fistula in ano) and Nasura (fistulous tracts). Its strong shodhana (cleansing) and ropana (wound healing) properties make it an effective preparation for management of chronic sinus tracts and fistulous conditions when used according to classical Ayurvedic principles.
